newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Protesters occupy Nicaraguan vote-counting site.
newsitem.headline: Protesters occupy Nicaraguan vote-counting site.

text.p: About 50 angry left-wing Sandinista protesters shouting "no more fraud!" occupied the vote-counting centre in Managua on Saturday, demanding authorities end alleged fraud in the count for Nicaragua's Oct. 20 general elections.
Dozens of armed, anti-riot police surrounding the centre gave the protesters 20 minutes to leave before they would move in.

Preliminary results from Nicaragua's disputed Oct. 20 vote gave Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance a 49 percent to 38 percent lead over former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega with 87 percent of the vote counted.

But the Sandinistas and several small parties have charged the vote was riddled with "serious irregularities," hinting at Liberal fraud, and are waiting for Nicaragua's Supreme Election Council (CSE) to review the count.
The CSE has said the winners will not be announced until mid- or late-November.
The delay in announcing the winners, and charges of fraud and irresponsibility being thrown between the bitter political rivals, have threatened to spark social unrest.
